html:
The map's name, from 300 to 100 BCE, for the Maurya Empire, the first state to rule most of the Indian subcontinent. It was founded around 322 BCE by Chandragupta Maurya in Magadha and ruled from Pataliputra.

Chandragupta overthrew the Nanda kings and took the north-west after Alexander left. His son Bindusara pushed south into the Deccan. His grandson Ashoka conquered Kalinga in the bloody Kalinga War around 261 BCE, then turned to Buddhism and carved his edicts on rocks and pillars across the empire.

The empire was large but loosely held beyond its core cities. After Ashoka it shrank, and in 185 BCE the general Pushyamitra killed the last Maurya king and founded the Shunga dynasty. The map's 100 BCE snapshot keeps the old name for lands that by then had passed to the Shungas and others.
